data.title: EMEA Morning Briefing: AI Bust Continues
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Watch For:

Eurozone flash consumer confidence indicator, France monthly business survey; no major trading updates expected

Opening Call:

European stock futures were lower, after Asia stocks fell. The yield on U.S. Treasurys fell, the dollar weakened. Gold fell and oil edged higher.

Equities:

European equity futures fell, after stocks on Wall Street closed lower in a volatile session as Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to staunch the bleeding in artificial-intelligence stocks.

"The deepening correction in tech stocks-which was unrelieved by the record-smashing IPO-is casting some doubt on just how much further the [Federal Reserve] will tighten," BMO's chief economist Douglas Porter said.

"While Fed officials continue to sound quite hawkish, softening equities will tighten financial conditions and could limit the extent of rate hikes."

Forex:

The U.S. dollar weakened and may face risk-off sentiment spurred by Wall Street's slide overnight.

"Risk-off is really the sentiment," Andrew Wells, chief investment officer at SanJac Alpha said. "I think we're seeing that kind of play out with Anthropic's IPO opening," as the initial euphoria cooled down during the trading session, he said.

Weakness in equities, in turn, could have implications for monetary policy.

Bonds:

The yield on U.S. Treasurys were edged lower as the Anthropic IPO failed to sustain risk appetite in Wall Street.

The debut on Nasdaq values the AI company at nearly $1.5 trillion, but it doesn't keep investors from rotating away from risky assets. The resulting demand for Treasurys pressures down yields even as markets price in a cycle of Fed hikes.

"The 10-year [Treasury] yield is still well over 5% and the small move down over the past week is indicative of a flight to safety," said Cardiff's Dean Lyulkin.

Energy:

Oil prices rose slightly amid Middle East tensions. A projectile launched by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels struck the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia's capital on Thursday.

"Uncertainty around the sustainability of strong Middle East exports could keep oil prices more elevated for longer than expected," said Citi Research analyst Xiaodan Zhu.

Metals:

Gold prices were lower, with silver falling to their lowest levels in over a year as the precious metals were weighed by growing expectations higher interest rates globally.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for the yellow metal as a safe haven for risk-averse investors.

Elevated Treasury yields and a strong dollar are raising the cost of holding the nonyielding yellow metal, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed that nearly all policymakers expected further interest rate increases will be needed, while weak gold exchange-traded fund flows in recent weeks have added to the subdued investment backdrop, he said

Copper fell to an eight-month low on a likely technical correction after settling higher in the previous session.

Chinese smelters were facing tight concentrate supply, said Zaye Capital Markets analyst Naeem Aslam.

The metal's price direction will likely depend on whether improving Chinese physical demand can offset softening global economic expectations and tighter financial conditions, he added.

TODAY'S TOP HEADLINES

Anthropic's IPO Is a Win for Venture. Its Success Could Reshape the Industry.

Venture backers finally stand to mint returns on the enormous amounts of capital they poured into Anthropic, cementing the idea that making bigger bets in pursuit of even bigger outcomes can pay off.

Anthropic's initial public offering could create lasting change in venture capital, a sector that has evolved to meet the needs of artificial-intelligence startups. Indeed, the company is slated to generate billions of dollars in returns for venture investors. Shares of the company were priced at $83 Wednesday evening, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

U.S. Has Floated NATO Membership for Ukraine in Recent Meetings

In closed-door peace talks over the past few months, President Trump's son-in-law and special envoy Jared Kushner has discussed an idea once believed to be dead-on-arrival: NATO membership for Ukraine if it cedes territory to Russia, said people familiar with the matter.

Moscow has fought for years to prevent Ukraine from joining the 32-member North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Trump himself ruled out NATO membership for Ukraine early last year as unacceptable to Russia.

TPG, Corpay to Buy Finance Platform Bill for About $6 Billion

Finance platform Bill Holdings will be acquired in a deal valued at about $6 billion, with TPG set to buy a majority stake and Corpay agreeing to buy a minority interest.

Starboard Value, Bill's largest stockholder, has agreed to vote in favor of the $63.25-a-share deal.

data.title: Trip.Best Unveils Its Biggest Global Rankings Yet, Covering All Seven Continents for the First Time
data.description:
Trip.Best Unveils Its Biggest Global Rankings Yet, Covering All Seven Continents for the First Time

Trip.Best Unveils Its Biggest Global Rankings Yet, Covering All Seven Continents for the First Time

PR Newswire

SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026

Global travel rankings grow to 98 annual lists across nine regions and 22 languages, with the first standalone Oceania lists.

SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trip.Best, the global travel rankings from Trip.com Group, launched its 2027 Annual Rankings in Sydney, extending coverage to all seven continents for the first time. Unveiled at The Dome, Sydney Showground, as part of Trip.com Group's Global Partner Summit, this year's edition grows from 85 to 98 annual rankings and from five to nine regions, across 22 languages.

Oceania, Africa and Antarctica join as new regions, and the Americas are now split into North and South America. In total, the 2027 Annual Rankings feature more than 3,700 entries across 112 countries and regions, spanning hotels, attractions, nightlife, dining and destinations. Winners were recognised at the Global 100 Awards Ceremony.

Oceania Steps Into the Global Spotlight With Eight Standalone Rankings

For the first time, Trip.Best publishes eight standalone Oceania 50 lists, recognising more than 250 hotels, attractions, restaurants and experiences across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands. The lists cover scenic hotels, must-see and family attractions, nightlife, fine dining and must-visit restaurants, with ski-resort and hot-spring rankings reflecting the region's year-round appeal.

Top-ranked winners include:

  • Scenic Hotel: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora, followed by Park Hyatt Sydney and Rosewood Kauri Cliffs in New Zealand.
  • Best Things to Do: Sydney Opera House, followed by Bora Bora and the TSS Earnslaw Steamship in Queenstown.
  • Fine Dining: Essence in Queenstown, followed by Bennelong in Sydney and Jano Bistro in Wellington.
  • Must-Visit Restaurant: Fergburger in Queenstown, followed by Bar Totti's in Sydney and Depot in Auckland.

Global 100 Lists Honour Leading Hotels, Sights and Restaurants

At global level, the Global 100 lists are led by:

  • Luxury Hotel: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel in Paris, followed by Raffles Singapore and Le Bristol Paris.
  • Scenic Hotel: Il San Pietro di Positano in Italy, followed by Cheval Blanc Randheli in the Maldives and Le Sirenuse in Positano.
  • Best Things to Do: The Louvre in Paris.
  • Fine Dining: DiverXO in Madrid, followed by L'Arpège in Paris and Disfrutar in Barcelona.

New Wonders Lists Showcase What Makes a Destination Distinctive

Trip.Best also introduces Wonders - a new collection of rankings aimed at international travellers seeking inspiration for their next destination. Each list is built on what makes a destination distinctive and what gives it an edge over others across markets. The collection comprises 49 themed lists across 10 countries and four categories (hotels, attractions, food and destinations) and is available in 22 languages.

Australia features in two lists: Native Wildlife Conservation Encounters, led by Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary, and Outdoor Adventures, led by Cairns. Global Wonders lists include Diving Experiences, Ski Towns and Sunset Views.

  • Explore the full Trip.Best 2027 rankings here

About Trip.com Group

Trip.com Group is a leading global travel service provider comprising of Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner, and Qunar. Across its platforms, Trip.com Group helps travellers around the world make informed and cost-effective bookings for travel products and services and enables partners to connect their offerings with users through the aggregation of comprehensive travel-related content and resources, and an advanced transaction platform consisting of apps, websites and 24/7 customer service centres. Founded in 1999 and listed on NASDAQ in 2003 and HKEX in 2021, Trip.com Group has become one of the best-known travel groups in the world, with the mission "to pursue the perfect trip for a better world". Find out more about Trip.com Group here: group.trip.com. Follow us on: X, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube.

data.title: Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders
data.description:
Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders

Neugebauer: Texas Court Ruling on Fermi's 70/30 Boardroom Maneuver Is a Loss for 100% of Texas Shareholders

PR Newswire

DALLAS, Nov. 19, 2026
  • Neugebauer: Under this ruling, the board can entrench itself with one quick vote, while shareholders need 70% of all outstanding shares to fight back.
  • Neugebauer: "That isn't Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."
  • Directors who failed to win a majority on October 30 are still sitting in the boardroom.
  • Neugebauer filing appeal because Texas's standing as the best place to do business in America depends on getting this right.
  • Texan voters have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them.

DALLAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toby Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (d/b/a Fermi America) (Nasdaq: FRMI) ("Fermi" or the "Company"), today issued the following statement after the Texas Business Court dismissed his claims in Neugebauer v. Fermi Inc. challenging the 70% supermajority bylaw the Company's board adopted in May without a shareholder vote.

"This isn't just a loss for Melissa and me. I believe it's a loss for every shareholder of every Texas company," said Toby Neugebauer. "Under this ruling, a board can change the rules in the middle of a fight, without a shareholder vote. It takes the board one quick vote to change the rules. It takes shareholders 70% of all outstanding shares to have a voice. Do the math. A little over 30% can block anything, and a share that is never voted counts as a no.

"Directors who could not win a majority of the shareholder support are still sitting in the boardroom. I don't think that is Texas-style good governance. It's entrenchment."

On May 13, 2026, in the middle of a shareholder contest, Fermi's board amended the Company's bylaws. Under the amendment, shareholders now need 70% of all outstanding shares to expand the board or change how the bylaws are amended. The board, however, can change those same rules with a simple majority vote of its directors. In August, the board changed director elections to require a majority of all outstanding shares, with unvoted shares counting as a no vote. At the October 30 annual meeting, neither director on the ballot reached that majority. Both men remain on the board.

"I'm proud of the work Texas has done to become the best place in America to do business," Neugebauer continued. "But capital flows to boards that answer to their owners. If shareholders can be silenced whenever a board disagrees with them, investors will notice."

This November, voters rejected the insider, pay-to-play politics that has harmed Fermi. Texans have made it clear that they don't accept that people in power can do whatever they want and change the rules whenever it suits them. We respectfully disagree with the Court and feel confident that we will be successful on appeal, because this isn't how good governance works.

Texas earned its business reputation. Now it has to protect it. I will continue to advocate for good governance, not for financial gain, but for the good of Texas.

SOURCE Toby Neugebauer

data.title: NetEase, Kuaishou Shares Plunge After 3Q Results Miss Estimates
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

Shares of Chinese internet companies NetEase and Kuaishou Technology fell Friday after their respective quarterly results missed consensus estimates.

NetEase's Hong Kong-listed stock plunged as much as 20% to 150.30 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$19.16, before paring losses to trade 18% lower. The stock remains on track for its largest one-day percentage decline since 2023, according to LSEG data.

Its American depository receipts closed 11% lower overnight.

Meanwhile, Kuaishou shares shed as much as 13% to HK$19.97, marking a record intraday low for the stock. It has since recouped some losses to trade 10% lower.

Earnings of both companies released Thursday failed to meet analysts' consensus projections. NetEase, China's second-largest gaming company, reported a 2.6% on-year decline in quarterly profit to 8.40 billion yuan, equivalent to $1.26 billion, versus market expectations of 9.45 billion yuan.

Analysts noted that softer-than-expected games segment revenue was the main drag on results. Growth in China's gaming market has moderated in the second half of the year following a strong start, partly due to a high base for PC games and a lack of blockbuster releases during the critical summer holiday season.

Despite the results miss, analysts at Citi and Nomura remain moderately optimistic about NetEase's outlook, pointing to the company's upcoming game title, "Ananta," slated for release in early 2027, as a potential key catalyst for future growth and revenue.

Meanwhile, short video platform operator Kuaishou swung to a wider-than-expected loss in the third quarter, weighed down by intense external competition and a changing consumer environment.

Citi analysts expressed a more cautious view on Kuaishou's prospects amid a tougher macroeconomic backdrop, intensified competition, and platform traffic pressures.

"We see limited visibility on Kuaishou's topline and profit trajectory ahead, though its net cash position could provide share price support," they said.

data.title: Point72 Asset Management, L.P. Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Personal Data Is Exposed
data.description:
Point72 Asset Management, L.P. Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Personal Data Is Exposed

Point72 Asset Management, L.P. Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Personal Data Is Exposed

PR Newswire

NEWTOWN, Pa., Nov. 19, 2026

National class action law firm offers free, confidential case evaluations to individuals whose information was held by Point72 Asset Management, L.P. and others whose personal information may have been exposed in the reported data breach.

NEWTOWN, Pa., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Edelson Lechtzin LLP, a national class action law firm, is investigating data privacy claims arising from a reported data breach at Point72 Asset Management, L.P. Anyone who has received a data breach notice from Point72 Asset Management, L.P. or who believes their personal information may have been exposed can request a free case evaluation.

Point72 Asset Management, L.P. data breach — at a glance

  • Company: Point72 Asset Management, L.P. ("Point72") is a global alternative investment firm founded in 2014 by Steven A. Cohen.
  • Reported: The company notified affected individuals by letter, and the incident was reported to the Massachusetts Attorney General.
  • How it reportedly happened: The breach occurred through a social engineering attack, in which an unauthorized third party compromised two Point72 user accounts and used them to copy certain files from limited portions of Point72's IT systems.
  • Who may be affected: Individuals whose personal information Point72 held, including information Point72 received from third parties in connection with investments its affiliates were considering.
  • Status: Certain details of the incident, including its full scope and the attacker's identity, remain unconfirmed or have not been publicly detailed.
  • Cost to you: Nothing. Click here for a free evaluation.

What Happened

Point72 experienced a social engineering incident in which an unauthorized third party compromised two Point72 user accounts, the first on July 31, 2026, and the second on August 3, 2026. The unauthorized party used the accounts to copy certain files containing personal information from limited portions of Point72's IT systems. Point72 says it discovered the unauthorized access on August 1 and August 4, 2026, respectively, contained it, engaged outside data security experts, and notified law enforcement.

What Personal Information May Be at Risk

Based on public accounts and regulatory filings, the information potentially involved varies by individual. The information that may have been compromised includes Social Security numbers and financial account numbers.

Who May Be Affected

The investigation focuses on Point72 Asset Management, L.P. and individuals who were affected by this breach. Anyone who has received a data breach notification connected to this incident may face an increased risk of identity theft and fraud and is encouraged to come forward.

Your Legal Options

Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating a potential class action to pursue legal remedies on behalf of individuals whose sensitive personal data may have been compromised in the reported breach. A successful case could recover compensation for losses such as lost time, out-of-pocket costs, and loss of privacy. It could push Point72 Asset Management, L.P. to strengthen how it protects personal information. The firm will evaluate your rights and potential claims at no cost.

Recommended Steps to Protect Yourself

NEWTOWN, Pa., Nov. 19, 2026

National class action law firm offers free, confidential case evaluations to Baker Tilly Advisory Group clients, parents or guardians of affected minors, and others whose personal information may have been exposed in the reported data breach.

NEWTOWN, Pa., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Edelson Lechtzin LLP, a national class action law firm, is investigating data privacy claims arising from a reported data breach at Baker Tilly Advisory Group. Anyone who has received a data breach notice from Baker Tilly Advisory Group or who believes their personal information may have been exposed can request a free case evaluation.

Baker Tilly Advisory Group data breach — at a glance

  • Company: Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP ("Baker Tilly") is a U.S. business advisory and tax firm serving middle-market companies across more than 30 industries and a member of the Baker Tilly International network.
  • Reported: The company sent notice letters to affected individuals and reported the incident to the Texas Attorney General's office on or about November 10, 2026.
  • How it reportedly happened: An unauthorized actor obtained data relating to certain Baker Tilly clients that was stored on a platform operated by a third-party service provider that Baker Tilly uses in providing services to clients.
  • Who may be affected: Baker Tilly clients, including minors.
  • Status: Certain details of the incident, including its full scope, the identity of the service provider, and the attacker's identity, remain unconfirmed or have not been publicly detailed.
  • Cost to you: Nothing. Click here for a free evaluation.

What Happened

Baker Tilly Advisory Group reported a data breach after an unauthorized actor obtained sensitive client information stored on a third-party service provider's platform. Baker Tilly says it became aware of the incident on September 6, 2026, and completed its review of the affected data on October 28, 2026. The company says it contained the incident, engaged third-party experts, and notified law enforcement.

What Personal Information May Be at Risk

Based on public accounts and regulatory filings, the information potentially involved varies by individual. The information that may have been compromised includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and other sensitive information.

Who May Be Affected

The investigation focuses on Baker Tilly Advisory Group and individuals who were affected by this breach. Anyone who has received a data breach notification connected to this incident may face an increased risk of identity theft and fraud and is encouraged to come forward.

Your Legal Options

Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating a potential class action to pursue legal remedies on behalf of individuals whose sensitive personal data may have been compromised in the reported breach. A successful case could recover compensation for losses such as lost time, out-of-pocket costs, and loss of privacy. It could push Baker Tilly Advisory Group to strengthen how it protects personal information. The firm will evaluate your rights and potential claims at no cost.

Recommended Steps to Protect Yourself

  • Review your account statements and credit reports regularly and stay alert for suspicious activity.
  • Confirm whether your information was involved in the Baker Tilly Advisory Group incident.
  • Preserve any letters or emails you received about the breach.
  • Baker Tilly's notice letter offers two years of complimentary credit and identity monitoring through Experian; consider enrolling before the deadline stated in your letter, and consider placing a fraud alert or security freeze with the three major credit bureaus.
